<a id="ingredient-identity-and-scope"></a>
## What counts as catfish

<a id="hmi-ing-001"></a>
<a id="what-commodity-biological-species-edible-part-and-commercial-forms-does-this-page-cover"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-002"></a>
<a id="which-processing-states-and-derivatives-are-distinct-materials-rather-than-synonyms"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-003"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-can-be-transferred-between-those-materials-and-what-requires-a-separate-answer"></a>

This page covers catfish in 3 forms kept separate in every comparison: catfish, as sold (198 results), catfish, oil (9 results) and catfish, cooked (3 results).<sup <div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-catfish" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-catfish-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of catfish, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

Counts describe evidence units, not independent studies or certainty.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Contributing family</th><th scope="col">Reference units</th><th scope="col">Weight</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Jianying et al. 2006</td><td>1</td><td>100%</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Methods</p><p>HMI pools subgroup medians for catfish, as sold on a as sold, as eaten or fresh weight basis: monitoring results summarized as one median per reporting region, sampling type and collection year, total diet composites and printed sample values as single observations, and printed subgroup medians from ordinary farms or markets. Each sampling family has equal total weight. Non-detects stay as zero-to-limit intervals, so quartiles carry lower and upper bounds. Means, ranges and maxima never enter as observations. Other forms, other bases, targeted sampling and results from mining, industrial, wastewater-affected, experimental, fertiliser or manufacturer settings are kept out of this reference.</p><p>Inverse weighted empirical CDF; midpoint at exact cumulative-weight boundaries. At least four reference units and a definitely positive Q1 to Q3 spread are required. This is a display eligibility rule, not statistical validation.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Limitations</p><p>Jianying et al. 2006 is the only compatible sampling family for catfish, as sold on this basis in the completed catfish ledger, so this single-family reference cannot represent other markets. Reporting regions and purchase markets are not growing areas. Non-detects with differing limits widen the bounds. Targeted catfish, as sold samples in PAHO had total mercury lower at 7.1 µg/kg, against 10 µg/kg for PAHO in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

In one study, total arsenic across 5 groups of catfish ranged from 42 µg/kg (Nandail (Kalai) river fish) to 524 µg/kg (Tulshiganga (Akkelpur) river fish); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/authors2022-arsenic-contamination-in-soil-vegetable-groundwater-and-riverine|10]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Unknown authors · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/authors2022-arsenic-contamination-in-soil-vegetable-groundwater-and-riverine">Arsenic Contamination in Soil, Vegetable, Groundwater, and Riverine Fish</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Peer-reviewed article</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/authors2022-arsenic-contamination-in-soil-vegetable-groundwater-and-riverine">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In another study, nickel across 4 groups of catfish ranged from 750 µg/kg (landing site Jangwani ziwani) to 800 µg/kg (landing site Mfulo wa Ng'ombe); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/sawe2023-fish-metals-lake-manyara-tanzania|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Sawe S, Amasi A, Wynants M · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/sawe2023-fish-metals-lake-manyara-tanzania">Assessment of Potentially Toxic Metals in Fish from Lake Manyara, Northern Tanzania</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Bulletin of Environmental Contamination and Toxicology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/sawe2023-fish-metals-lake-manyara-tanzania">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

## Trade-offs and limits of controls

<a id="hmi-ing-022"></a>
<a id="can-an-intervention-increase-another-contaminant-or-redistribute-contamination-to-a-by-product"></a>

<a id="what-costs-constraints-adverse-effects-or-failure-modes-are-documented-and-which-are-unknown"></a>

Metals do not move together, so a lot that passes a lead limit says little about cadmium, arsenic or nickel unless those are tested as well.



<a id="sampling-and-testing"></a>
## Testing catfish for metals

<a id="hmi-ing-025"></a>
<a id="what-sampling-design-is-appropriate-for-the-ingredient-heterogeneity-lot-and-decision"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-026"></a>

<a id="what-can-a-certificate-of-analysis-or-non-detect-establish-and-what-remains-untested"></a>

Results depend on the method and its reporting limit. Reporting limits for lead ranged from 3 µg/kg (WHO GEMS/Food) to 3,000 µg/kg (WHO GEMS/Food), so a non-detect from a less sensitive method says much less.<sup <details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-origins-or-products-of-catfish-measured-lowest" data-anchor="which-origins-or-products-of-catfish-measured-lowest" data-question="Which origins or products of catfish measured lowest?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which origins or products of catfish measured lowest?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In one study, total arsenic across 5 groups of catfish ranged from 42 µg/kg (Nandail (Kalai) river fish) to 524 µg/kg (Tulshiganga (Akkelpur) river fish); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/authors2022-arsenic-contamination-in-soil-vegetable-groundwater-and-riverine|10]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Unknown authors · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/authors2022-arsenic-contamination-in-soil-vegetable-groundwater-and-riverine">Arsenic Contamination in Soil, Vegetable, Groundwater, and Riverine Fish</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Peer-reviewed article</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/authors2022-arsenic-contamination-in-soil-vegetable-groundwater-and-riverine">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In another study, nickel across 4 groups of catfish ranged from 750 µg/kg (landing site Jangwani ziwani) to 800 µg/kg (landing site Mfulo wa Ng'ombe); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/sawe2023-fish-metals-lake-manyara-tanzania|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Sawe S, Amasi A, Wynants M · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/sawe2023-fish-metals-lake-manyara-tanzania">Assessment of Potentially Toxic Metals in Fish from Lake Manyara, Northern Tanzania</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Bulletin of Environmental Contamination and Toxicology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/sawe2023-fish-metals-lake-manyara-tanzania">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-catfish-is-inorganic" data-anchor="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-catfish-is-inorganic" data-question="How much of the arsenic in catfish is inorganic?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How much of the arsenic in catfish is inorganic?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Inorganic arsenic, the more toxic form, was measured in 2 results from 1 source, far fewer than total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> WHO GEMS/Food submissions reported inorganic arsenic in catfish, as sold from 2 results in 2 reporting regions, with subgroup medians below 20 µg/kg, mostly non-detects.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>
